item.title: Taking a Trip to the Maldives to Observe a Presidential Election… A Business Trip to Florence to Watch On-Site Vote Counting (대선 참관한다며 몰디브 가고… 현장 개표 본다며 피렌체 출장)
item.description:
Taking a Trip to the Maldives to Observe a Presidential Election… A Business Trip to Florence to Watch On-Site Vote Counting (대선 참관한다며 몰디브 가고… 현장 개표 본다며 피렌체 출장)

In November 2025, five Grade 5–7 employees from local election commissions in the Yeongnam region took a nine-day business trip to Rome and Florence, Italy. The theme was "Research on Introducing On-Site Vote Counting at Polling Stations in Italy." Italy has about 60,000 polling stations—four times the number in South Korea—where votes are counted directly at the polling stations. In contrast, South Korea collects ballot boxes at separate counting centers. The trip team stated in their report, "Since on-site vote counting at polling stations is institutionally impossible in South Korea, the feasibility of introduction will be examined under the premise that relevant laws can be amended." They noted that to operate polling stations like Italy, South Korea would need an additional 45,000 polling stations and 390,000 election and counting staff. <<> In September 2023, ten election commission employees also visited Rome, Florence, and Venice in Italy for an eight-night, nine-day training session with the theme "Studying the Political Status of Italian Youth to Find Ways to Boost Political Participation Among South Korean Youth." They interviewed five university students, but other interviewees included one member of the lower house of parliament, four city council chairs and staff, and five city hall election officials. The remaining schedule was noted as "organizing collected data" and "discussion." <<> These two cases are part of the 62 official overseas business trips and training sessions over the past three years that the election commission has disclosed on its website. By country, the destinations included the United States (8 times), Germany (5 times), Canada and Sweden (4 each), and Japan, Norway, and Malaysia (3 each). There were also instances of trips to the Maldives to observe local presidential elections or to Switzerland to derive improvements for referendums. A political source commented, "The election commission can go on overseas trips if necessary, but it's questionable how many actually lead to tangible policy outcomes." <<> The necessity of the election commission's overseas deployment of employees for "overseas election management" has also been a subject of controversy. First introduced in 2012 with the launch of overseas voting for nationals abroad, these employees are tasked with encouraging overseas voting and supporting the voting process ahead of presidential and general elections. Their stays range from as short as two months to as long as three years. Ahead of last year's presidential election, the commission deployed 18 people to 18 cities in 8 countries. For the 2024 general election, 22 employees were sent abroad. At that time, the average budget per overseas election manager was 150 million won. In total, 176 election commission employees have been dispatched overseas since 2011. <<> The election commission emphasizes the necessity of these dispatches, noting that overseas missions with deployed staff handle over 60% of all overseas voters. However, diplomatic missions without deployed election commission employees also conduct overseas voting. Within the government, questions have been raised about the need for long-term overseas election managers. <<> Employees deployed overseas as election managers do not even need foreign language skills. This is because the election commission has requested that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs waive language requirements for dispatched staff, citing reasons such as "election management skills are more important than foreign language ability" and "we provide services to overseas nationals who speak Korean." <<> The election commission is also regarded as one of the fastest-growing institutions in terms of organizational size. The commission's staff count was 1,987 in 1996, but it increased by 52.7% to 3,034 people over 30 years. With the National Election Commission, 17 metropolitan and provincial election commissions, about 250 district-level election commissions, and over 3,500 town, township, and neighborhood election commissions, there are more than 23,000 non-standing committee members who receive allowances. The annual expenditure of the election commission was 292 billion won in 2015, but it rose to 363.4 billion won (budget-based) last year, an increase of 24.4% over the decade. (2025년 11월 영남 지역 시·군·구 선거관리위원회 소속 5~7급 직원 5명은 이탈리아 로마와 피렌체로 9일간 출장에 나섰다. 주제는 ‘이탈리아의 투표소 현장 개표 도입 방안 연구’. 이탈리아는 투표소가 한국의 4배인 6만여 곳으로, 투표소에서 바로 개표를 한다. 반면 한국은 별도 개표소에 투표함을 모아 개표를 한다. 출장팀은 보고서에서 “(한국은) 투표소 현장 개표는 제도적으로 불가하므로 관련 법규는 개정이 가능하다는 전제하에 도입 가능성을 검토한다”고 했다. 그러면서 한국이 이탈리아처럼 투표소를 운영하려면 투표소 4만5000개, 투·개표 인력 39만명이 더 필요하다고 했다.)

item.title: [Episode 13] The One Line That Brought a Chaebol Chairman to a Halt ([13화] 재벌 회장을 주저앉힌 한 마디)
item.description:
[Episode 13] The One Line That Brought a Chaebol Chairman to a Halt ([13화] 재벌 회장을 주저앉힌 한 마디)

☞ View from Episode 1 (☞ 1화부터 보기)

☞ Character Introduction (☞ 등장인물 소개)

Chairman Shin Jae-hyuk turned his back on the chalet at Seongnam Airport and headed toward a black limousine waiting on one side of the runway. His steps were resolute, and the wall of aides surrounding him was formidable. The distance to Evan was about 15 meters. If Chairman Shin took just five more steps, the car door would open, and after that, it would become difficult to even speak to him. (신재혁 회장이 성남공항의 샬레를 등지고 활주로 한편에 대기 중인 검은색 리무진을 향했다. 발걸음은 단호했고, 신 회장을 에워싼 수행원들의 벽은 견고했다. 에반과의 거리는 약 15미터 정도였다. 신 회장이 다섯 걸음만 더 나가면 차 문이 열리고, 그 뒤로는 더는 말을 걸기 어려워질 상황이었다.)

There was only one way to break through that wall. (그 벽을 뚫을 방법은 단 하나뿐이었다.)

"Shin Jae-hyuk!" (“신재혁!”)

Evan's shout pierced through the lingering echo of the jet engines and struck Chairman Shin's back. (에반의 외침이 제트 엔진의 잔향을 뚫고 신 회장의 등에 꽂혔다.)

Two aides flinched and turned around at the disrespectful address coming from somewhere. Just as one of them moved to block Evan with an angry expression, Chairman Shin silently raised his hand. All the aides froze. (수행원 두 명이 어디선가 들려온 불경한 호칭에 흠칫 돌아섰다. 한 명이 성난 표정으로 에반의 앞을 막아서려는 순간, 신 회장이 말없이 손을 들었다. 수행원들 모두 얼어붙었다.)

Chairman Shin slowly turned around and began to scan Evan. It was the same gaze from a few days ago in the Pangyo office, which had coldly regarded him, saying, "Caution and indecisiveness are different." (신 회장은 천천히 몸을 돌려 에반의 모습을 훑기 시작했다. 며칠 전, 판교 집무실에서 “신중함과 우유부단함은 다릅니다”라며 차갑게 바라봤던 그 눈빛이었다.)

Evan did not flinch. (에반은 피하지 않았다.)

"Are you satisfied with merely the title of 'Asia's subcontractor' as you get into that car?" (“고작 ‘아시아의 하청업체’라는 타이틀에 만족하며 차에 오르시는 겁니까?”)

Though tension was evident on the faces of the two aides, Chairman Shin instead began to listen. (두 수행원의 얼굴에 긴장감이 역력했지만, 신 회장은 되려 귀를 기울이기 시작했다.)

"Taesan Defense's achievements are remarkable. But to the Western defense giants with over a century of history, Taesan is still just a 'cost-effective hardware factory.'" (“태산디펜스가 이룬 성취는 경이롭습니다. 하지만 100년 넘는 역사를 가진 서구 방산 거물들에게, 태산은 여전히 ‘가성비 좋은 하드웨어 공장’입니다.”)

Evan took another step closer. As an aide moved to stop him again, Chairman Shin gestured for them to halt. (에반이 한 걸음 더 다가섰다. 수행원이 다시 제지하려 하자, 신 회장은 수행원을 향해 멈추라고 손짓을 했다.)

"Sentinel offering the code isn't a partnership. It means they're hiring you, Chairman, as a high-end mechanic to maintain their outdated engines." (“센티넬이 코드를 주겠다고 한 것은 파트너십이 아닙니다. 회장님을 본인들의 낡은 엔진을 관리해 줄 고급 정비공으로 고용하겠다는 뜻입니다.”)

Chairman Shin's expression did not change. His steps stopped right in front of the limousine. Evan seized the opportunity. (신 회장의 표정이 변하지 않았다. 발걸음이 리무진 바로 앞에서 멈췄다. 에반은 그 틈을 놓치지 않았다.)

"You know better than anyone, Chairman. Starting with Philip Exeter, following the same training as them, conversing in the same way of thinking, perfectly completing the elite course they designed, barely getting into the secret clubs..." (“회장님은 누구보다 잘 아실 겁니다. 필립 엑서터부터 시작해 그들과 같은 교정을 밟고, 같은 사고 방식으로 대화하고, 그들이 만든 엘리트 코스를 완벽하게 밟고, 비밀 클럽에도 간신히 들어가셨겠지만…")

Evan wove Chairman Shin's confidential personal information into the conversation as if it were common knowledge. (에반은 신 회장의 기밀 신상 정보를 상식처럼 대화에 엮어 넣었다.)

"Has that inner circle ever truly accepted you as an equal?" (“그 이너 서클이 회장님을 진정으로 동등한 일원으로 받아준 적이 있습니까?”)

At the mention of his past, the muscles in Chairman Shin's face subtly tensed up. The information Jordan had shown in the Pyeongtaek parking lot was doing its job. It was the perfect time for a counterattack. (신 회장의 과거를 들먹이자 얼굴 근육이 미세하게 경직됐다. 조던이 평택 주차장에서 보여준 정보가 제 몫을 하고 있었다. 반격이 올 수 있는 타이밍이었다.)

Evan didn't give him any leeway. (에반은 틈을 주지 않았다.)

"Think about why Sentinel is willingly giving you the source code. Sentinel has never solved the latency gap issue. The moment you take over their unverified technology and algorithms, Taesan becomes a scapegoat workshop bearing all the errors and accident liability within it. You become subordinate to the illusion of ownership." (“센티넬이 순순히 소스코드를 준다는 이유를 곱씹어 보시죠. 센티넬은 레이턴시 갭(latency gap) 이슈를 해결한 적이 없습니다. 검증되지 않은 기술과 알고리즘을 넘겨 받는 순간, 태산은 그 안의 모든 오류와 사고 책임을 떠안는 독박 정비소가 됩니다. 소유권이라는 환상에 종속되는 겁니다.”)

Chairman Shin's eyes wavered for the first time. (신 회장의 눈빛이 처음으로 흔들렸다.)

[Technical Verification: Incomplete]. ([기술 검증: 미완료].)

The red text Evan had spotted on the table just before leaving Chairman Shin's office was the card he pulled out for this very moment. (에반이 신 회장의 집무실을 나서기 직전 테이블 위에서 포착했던 빨간 글씨는, 지금 이 순간 내밀기 위한 카드였다.)

"Is owning the source code localization? No. The battlefield is a living organism that changes in real time." (“소스코드를 소유해야 국산화입니까? 아닙니다. 전장은 실시간으로 변하는 생물입니다.”)

Evan pulled the Sariel authentication module from his pocket. The matte black metal absorbed the October sunlight. He held it up on his palm, showing it to Chairman Shin. (에반은 주머니에서 사리엘 인증 모듈을 꺼냈다. 무광 검정의 금속이 10월 햇살 아래에서도 빛을 흡수했다. 그는 그것을 신 회장에게 보이듯 손바닥 위에 올렸다.)

"Mount Taesan's hardware on top of Sariel. Manufacturing, integration, delivery—all under Taesan's name. Taesan will also develop the interface for the South Korean military. The Ministry of National Defense gets the justification of localization, and for the President, it becomes a successful export case for K-Defense." (“사리엘 위에 태산의 하드웨어를 태우십시오. 제조, 통합, 납품. 전부 태산 명의로. 한국군 인터페이스도 태산이 개발합니다. 국방부에는 국산화라는 명분이 서고, 대통령에게는 수출 가능한 K-방산의 성공 사례가 됩니다.”)

Evan said what he couldn't say in Pangyo. He poured out the business structure he had designed around 3 AM a few days ago. (에반은 판교에서 말하지 못했던 것을 말했다. 얼마 전 새벽 3시에 설계한 사업 구조를 쏟아냈다.)

"And what about the data?" (“그리고 데이터는요?”)

Chairman Shin spoke for the first time. Though his voice was low, the very question had opened the door to conversation. Evan's heart beat a little faster. When this question came up in Pangyo, Evan had said, "We need to review it." Indecisiveness. Today was different. (신 회장이 처음으로 입을 열었다. 목소리는 낮았지만, 질문 자체가 대화의 문을 연 것이었다. 에반의 심장이 한 박자 빨라졌다. 판교에서 이 질문이 나왔을 때, 에반은 “검토가 필요합니다”라고 말했다. 우유부단함. 오늘은 달랐다.)

"Data processing goes through the Dudaelle Cloud. That is non-negotiable." (“데이터 처리는 듀다엘 클라우드를 거칩니다. 그것은 바꿀 수 없습니다.”)

Chairman Shin let out a long exhale. (신 회장이 한 박자 길게 숨을 내쉬었다.)

"But—" (“하지만—")

Evan took another step closer. (에반이 한 걸음 더 다가섰다.)

"Sariel is real-time adaptive. It feeds on battlefield data and evolves. The more it operates on Taesan's hardware, the more precise it becomes, and over time, the gap with Sentinel will widen. If you request a comparative verification, Sariel will prove itself on the spot." (“사리엘은 실시간 적응형입니다. 전장 데이터를 먹고 진화합니다. 태산의 하드웨어 위에서 운용될수록 정밀해지고, 시간이 갈수록 센티넬과의 격차는 벌어집니다. 회장님이 비교 검증을 요청하시면, 사리엘은 그 자리에서 증명할 겁니다.”)

Evan began to get slightly excited. (에반이 살짝 흥분하기 시작했다.)

"You just have to wear the crown, Chairman. I'll bear the weight of it." (“회장님은 왕관만 쓰시면 됩니다. 왕관의 무게는 제가 지겠습니다.”)

Evan's short pitch was over. He steadied his breath again. (에반의 짧은 피칭이 끝났다. 에반은 숨을 다시 가라앉혔다.)

The echo of the jet engines faded away. Only the October wind flowed between the two men. (제트 엔진의 잔향이 사라졌다. 두 사람 사이에 10월의 바람만 흘렀다.)

Chairman Shin did not move. 5 seconds. 10 seconds. Evan did not move either. (신 회장이 움직이지 않았다. 5초. 10초. 에반도 움직이지 않았다.)

"...I don't think this is the place for negotiations." (“…여기가 협상할 자리는 아니라고 보는데요.")

Chairman Shin reached out and casually straightened Evan's tousled tie. (신 회장은 손을 뻗어 에반의 헝클어진 넥타이를 슬쩍 바로잡았다.)

"Next time we meet, mind your attire. You might be dealing with a potential partner." (“다음에 볼 땐 옷매무새 좀 신경 쓰세요. 파트너가 될지도 모르는 사람인데.”)

Leaving those words, Chairman Shin settled into the back seat of the limousine. (신 회장은 그 말을 남기고 리무진 뒷좌석에 몸을 실었다.)

Thud. (쿵.)

The car door closed. The black vehicle exited the runway, leaving Evan behind. (차 문이 닫혔다. 검은색 차량이 에반을 남겨둔 채 활주로를 빠져나갔다.)

Evan stood alone on the asphalt. The authentication module in his palm had been warmed by his body heat. It was no longer cold metal, but warm metal. (에반은 아스팔트 위에 홀로 섰다. 손바닥 위의 인증 모듈이 체온에 데워졌다. 차가운 금속이 아니라, 따뜻한 금속이었다.)

Inside the moving limousine, Chairman Shin stared for a moment at Evan's silhouette, receding through the window. In the shimmering heat of the runway, the suited man grew smaller and smaller. (달리는 리무진 안에서 신 회장은 창밖으로 멀어지는 에반의 실루엣을 잠시 응시했다. 활주로의 아지랑이 속에서 정장 차림의 남자가 점점 작아졌다.)

His executive secretary asked cautiously. (수행 비서가 조심스럽게 물었다.)

"Chairman, shall we proceed with the meeting with Sentinel as scheduled?" (“회장님, 센티넬 쪽 미팅은 예정대로 진행할까요?”)

Chairman Shin didn't answer. Instead, he took out his smartphone and sent a message to the head of public relations. (신 회장은 대답하지 않았다. 대신 스마트폰을 꺼내 홍보실장에게 메시지를 보냈다.)

[Shin: Send the press release V2 draft now.] ([신: 보도자료 V2 초안, 지금 보내.])

The answer to the secretary's question lay within that message. (비서의 질문에 대한 답은 그 메시지 안에 들어 있었다.)

V2—Version 2. (V2—버전 2.)

It meant that there existed an announcement prepared for a different scenario, not the V1 press release which had already assumed the partnership with Sentinel as a done deal. (센티넬과의 파트너십을 기정사실화한 V1 보도자료가 아닌, 다른 시나리오를 위해 준비해 둔 발표문이 존재했다는 뜻이었다.)

A faint smile crept onto Chairman Shin's lips. (신 회장의 입가에 살짝 미소가 걸렸다.)

He probably never considered Sentinel a 'real' partner from the beginning. Sentinel's technical verification was incomplete, and their characteristic Western corporate arrogance was off-putting. Sentinel had been a bargaining chip in negotiations with Dudaelle. A tool of pressure to soften the arrogant negotiating stance of Dudaelle—as arrogant as Sentinel—and a lever to extract more favorable terms from whoever broke through the wall. (그는 처음부터 센티넬을 ‘진짜’ 파트너로 생각하지 않았을 것이다. 센티넬의 기술 검증은 미완료였고, 서구 기업 특유의 거만함도 불쾌하게 따라붙었다. 센티넬은 듀다엘과의 협상을 미끼였던 것이다. 센티넬만큼 오만한 듀다엘의 오만한 협상 태도를 누그러뜨리기 위한 압박 도구이자, 그 벽을 뚫고 들어오는 자에게서 더 유리한 조건을 끌어내기 위한 지렛대였다.)

Perhaps Shin Jae-hyuk had been waiting for someone to break through that pressure and stand before him. (그 압박을 뚫고 자신의 앞에 서는 인간이 나타나기를, 신재혁은 기다리고 있었는지도 모른다.)

Chairman Shin turned his gaze from the window and looked down at his smartphone screen. The runway of Seongnam Airport receded outside the window. Evan's silhouette left behind on the asphalt was no longer visible. (신 회장은 창밖에서 고개를 돌려 스마트폰 화면을 내려다봤다. 창밖으로 성남 공항의 활주로가 멀어졌다. 아스팔트 위에 남겨진 에반의 실루엣은 이미 보이지 않았다.)

A reply came from the PR director. (홍보실장의 답장이 왔다.)

item.title: They can bind my body, but they cannot take my heart. (나의 몸을 묶을 순 있어도, 마음을 빼앗을 순 없다)
item.description:
They can bind my body, but they cannot take my heart. (나의 몸을 묶을 순 있어도, 마음을 빼앗을 순 없다)

On May 25, 1983, YS was forcibly taken to Seoul National University Hospital. It was the 8th day of his hunger strike under house arrest. A force of 300 police officers from Noryangjin Police Station surrounded his home and loaded him into an ambulance. (YS는 1983년 5월 25일 서울대병원으로 강제 이송됩니다. 가택 연금 중 단식 8일째를 맞은 날이었습니다. 노량진경찰서 병력 300명이 집 주위를 포위하고 YS를 앰뷸런스에 실었습니다.)

YS refused medical treatment and food at the hospital, continuing his hunger strike. Kwon Ik-hyun, the secretary-general of the ruling Democratic Justice Party and a classmate of President Chun Doo-hwan at the 11th class of the Korea Military Academy, visited his hospital room three times. Claiming that Chun was worried about YS’s health, he asked YS to end the hunger strike, saying, “We will pursue democracy.” (YS는 병원에서 진료와 음식을 거부하고 단식을 이어갑니다. 전두환 대통령의 육사 11기 동기인 집권 민정당 사무총장 권익현이 병실에 세 차례 찾아와 전두환이 YS의 건강을 걱정하고 있다면서 “민주주의를 할 것”이라며 단식 중단을 요청합니다.)

On the evening of May 29, Kwon visited again and notified YS, saying, “As of midnight tonight, your house arrest will be lifted.” Kwon conveyed, “You are free to do as you please—whether to go to England, Japan, or the United States.” He added that all of this was Chun Doo-hwan’s intention. (5월 29일 저녁에도 찾아와 “오늘 밤 12시를 기해 연금을 해제한다”고 통고했습니다. 권익현은 “무엇을 하든 자유이며 영국이든, 일본이든, 미국이든 가는 것도 자유”라고 전했습니다. 이 모두 전두환의 뜻이라고 덧붙였습니다.)

YS wrote, “When has the ruler or the government ever worried about my health? This is an audacious statement.” He continued to refuse medical treatment and food. The doctor said, “We simply cannot continue like this. I will administer an injection,” but YS did not yield. It was the 16th day of his hunger strike. (YS는 “집권자나 정부가 언제 나의 건강을 걱정했느냐. 뻔뻔스러운 이야기”라고 적었습니다. 진료와 음식을 계속 거부합니다. 의사가 “도저히 이런 상태로는 안 된다. 주사를 놓겠다”고 했지만 주장을 굽히지 않습니다. 단식 16일째가 지나고 있었습니다.)

Today is a day I can never forget. Around 9 a.m., under the direction of the Noryangjin Police Station chief, a total force of over 300 police officers completely surrounded my home, forcibly took away Jang and Chung-il, and I, with no other man present, was forcibly moved to Seoul National University Hospital in an ambulance alongside Dr. Seo from the university. Hye-suk accompanied me. (오늘은 영원(永遠)히 잊을 수 없는 날이다. 아침 9시경(時頃) 노량진경찰서장의 지휘로 총(總) 병력(兵力) 300여명(余名)은 우리집 주이(*위)를 완전히 포위하고 장(張)과 충일(忠一)이를 강제 연행해 가고 남자(男子)라고는 한 사람도 없는 가운데 서울대학(大學)의 서박사(徐博士)와 같이 와서 앤부란서(*앰뷸런스)로 강제로 서울대학(大學) 병원(病院)으로 옴(*옮)겨졌다. 나는 혜숙(惠淑)이와 동행(同行)이였다.)

It was the VIP room on the 12th floor of Seoul National University Hospital. Today marks the 8th day of my hunger strike. The doctors brought medical care and food to me, but I firmly refused everything. I even told the police chief who forcibly took me away, ‘You may be able to imprison me, place me under house arrest, kill me, or use violence against me as you please, but you cannot take away my heart.’ After I left, my home was completely occupied by police and intelligence agents, and the phone was disconnected for 7 hours from 10:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. <<> At 9:30 p.m., Kwon Ik-hyun came. He talked about how “Chun” was worried about my health. What a truly ridiculous story. When has the ruler or the government ever worried about my health? It’s a shameless claim. His request was simply for me to end the hunger strike because I was wrong, and he said that democracy would definitely be achieved. <<> It has been one night since I came to the hospital. Today as well, I continue to refuse medical treatment and food. <<> Hye-young, Lee Seo-bang, and Eun-cheol called from the United States, apparently very worried. Last night, my father suddenly came from Masan. He had come because intelligence agents visited him and said I was dying and had been moved to the hospital. I had been conversing well with him until now, but it turned out this way. My wife, Hyun-cheol, and Hye-suk persuaded him well, and he returned this afternoon. A fortunate thing. How must my father feel? How painful and distressing must it be for him, not even being able to see me? <<> Life at the hospital today remains the same. My wife, Hyun-cheol, and Hye-suk visited again today. <<> At 9:30 p.m., Kwon Ik-hyun came and went again. It was of course the same as yesterday. Now that the hunger strike has reached 10 days, I believe my intent is 90% achieved, so he asked me to accept medical treatment and food for my health. He pleaded. Of course, I firmly refused. He also talked about how without democracy, it would be impossible to maintain power in this country. <<> Today, it hasn’t rained, and although the sun shines, it’s not a pleasant day. Changgyeongwon looks beautiful beyond the window. <<> I think many young people who desire freedom and democracy in this land have been taken by the police today as well. I truly pray to God. I sincerely pray that this land may soon become a society with righteous freedom and democracy, a country where humans can live like humans. We cannot forget the historical lesson that violent politics will inevitably be destroyed by violence. <<> I have come to Seoul National University Hospital and am experiencing the Lord’s Day for the first time. <<> Today marks the 12th day of my hunger strike. <<> Various news is coming in from the United States. <<> It is said that starting tomorrow, Monday, many Korean-Americans will begin a hunger strike in front of the U.S. State Department. <<> And from June 4th, they will hold a demonstration in front of the White House. I hear this phone call came from Mr. Kim Seong-nam in the United States. <<> Around 11 a.m., Mr. Yoo Chi-song came, talked for about 40 minutes, and left. His talk concerned wanting me to take food and receive medical treatment for the sake of the country’s future and Chairman Kim’s health, and that he would make every effort with the government side in various ways. In the evening, Mr. Kwon Ik-hyun came and went again. <<> It was a notification that my house arrest would be lifted as of midnight. And he said that I was free to do anything, whether going to England, Japan, or the United States, completely free. He said all of this came from “Chun.” <<> In the morning, about 20 to 30 foreign correspondents came and went. In my room, I allowed them to take photos for just 3 to 4 minutes. Director Kim held a press conference on my behalf. <<> Many people came and went today. <<> Lee Min-woo, Park Young-rok, Jo Yoon-hyung, Vice President Lee Ki-taek, many former lawmakers, lawmakers such as Son Se-il, Seo Seok-jae, and Lee Jeong-bin, and many comrades came and went, shedding tears. <<> Pastor Park Hyung-kyu and Professor Lee Moon-young visited. From Chunghyun Church, Pastor Kim Won-nim, Jang Jeong-il, Kim Seong-geun, Pastor Lee Se-il, and several evangelists held a worship service and left. <<> Today marks the 2nd week of my hunger strike. <<> Many people visited again today. <<> Especially, Pastor Moon Ik-hwan’s parents, Pastor Moon’s wife, and Mr. Lee Moon-young’s wife visited. <<> Hye-young, bringing Gun-woo, rushed from the United States after suddenly hearing news about me. <<> Today marks the 15th day of my hunger strike. <<> Pastor Kim Chang-in visited. <<> At 3 p.m., 13 members of the Countermeasure Committee visited. <<> The 13 members include Lee Min-woo, Park Young-rok, Jo Yoon-hyung, Lee Ki-taek, Kim Nok-young, Kim Sang-hyeon, Hong Young-ki, Kim Myeong-yun, and others. It is said that about 70 people gathered at the Korea Hotel at 10 a.m. today and issued a Democratic National Salvation Declaration. <<> In it, they support the five demands I made and urge me to end my hunger strike. <<> ‘I said that while I appreciate your intentions, I cannot bend my resolve.’ <<> Today marks the 16th day of my hunger strike. <<> I declined all visits today because my body is suffering greatly. <<> A section chief, Deputy Section Chief Lee, and Dr. Seo came and said that physically, I have reached a limit today, and as doctors, they cannot allow this condition to continue. They declared that they would firmly administer an injection today. I firmly refused, saying I absolutely cannot receive an injection today. We talked for a long time, but I did not yield my position to the end. <<> In the end, they said they would return at 6:30 a.m. tomorrow and left. (서울 대학병원(大學病院) 12층(層) VIP실(室)이였다. 오늘로 단식 8일(日)째다. 의사들은 나에게 진료와 엄(*음)식을 가지고 와서나(*왔으나) 나는 단호히 모두 거절했다. 나는 나를 강제로 나를 연행(連行)하는 서장에게도 ‘너이(*희)들이 나를 형무소나 혹은 가택연금(家宅軟禁)을 하거나 죽이거(나) 폭력(力)으로 나를 마음대로 할 수는 있을지 모르지 마는 나의 마음을 빳(*뺏)아 갈 수는 없을 것이다’라고 말해주었다. 내가 나온 다음 우리집은 경찰과 정보원들에 위(*의)해서 완전히 점령되고 전화도 아침 10시(時) 30분(分)부터 5시(時) 30분(分)까지 7시간(時間) 동안 단절되었다.)
